scores.rationale: A low-cost serialization intervention directly tests whether placing continuation-predictive code distinctions earlier helps autoregressive SID generation. It preserves tokenizer assignments and adds essentially no training cost, making the causal comparison unusually clean.
scores.uncertainties: The proposed estimators are not fully consistent (PMI-style scoring versus conditional mutual information), and full-tuple conditioning may induce leakage-like redundancy or unstable estimates. Level scores may be tied, dominated by item frequency, or fail to matter because the generator can use all positions equally well.

scores.rationale: Covariance preconditioning has a plausible geometric rationale: Euclidean quantization can overemphasize high-variance axes. The transform is straightforward, train-only, and compatible with the existing pipeline, although it is a familiar preprocessing intervention rather than a substantially new quantizer.
scores.uncertainties: High-variance directions may encode useful semantics, while low-variance directions may mostly be noise. The specified eigenvalue floor and shrinkage may materially affect results; gains could reflect changed embedding scale or seed variation rather than better item distinctions.

scores.rationale: This is a feasible, testable covariance-whitening approach with a sound motivation about anisotropic embedding distances. Its core mechanism substantially overlaps the other covariance-preconditioning proposal, and the fixed transform leaves the modeling pipeline simple.
scores.uncertainties: The benefit depends on whether embedding anisotropy is nuisance variation rather than task-relevant structure. Whitening can amplify noisy directions; shrinkage choices and the relationship between reconstruction geometry and recommendation ranking remain uncertain.

scores.rationale: Stage-wise scaling is a concrete intervention on residual quantization dynamics that retains the codebook count and hard-assignment structure. It tests whether later stages are under-trained due to residual magnitude imbalance, with low computational overhead and measurable intermediate effects.
scores.uncertainties: Scaling both code vectors and residuals changes the effective balance of reconstruction, commitment, and codebook losses, so it may not isolate residual magnitude alone. Warm-up scales may become stale, and improved code usage or residual reduction may not translate into ranking gains.

scores.rationale: Appending a frozen, train-only position-role token is implementable and tests whether a simple behavioral attribute complements content-derived IDs. Its marginal sequence-position signal differs from changing quantizer geometry and can be evaluated without adding training-time model cost.
scores.uncertainties: Mean position may capture sequence construction or truncation artifacts rather than a stable item role. It ignores context and user heterogeneity, and the added token may be redundant with history input or fragment existing content prefixes, especially for sparse items.
